claims.claim: At a French STOP-controlled intersection, the driver must stop at the edge of the approached carriageway, then yield and enter only when safe.
French national default speed limits include 130 motorway, 110 divided carriageway and 80 other roads; rain reductions apply.
For fixed radars, retained speed deducts 5 km/h below 100 km/h or 5 percent above 100 km/h; the correction is larger for specified mobile systems.
Article 122 establishes administrative liability for exceeding the speed limit by more than 20 km/h, with a higher tier above 50 km/h.
Ukrainian sign 3.29 prohibits driving faster than the value shown.
At an otherwise uncontrolled French intersection, the driver arriving from the left must yield to the driver arriving from the right.
At an uncontrolled intersection of roads of equal priority in Ukraine, a driver yields to vehicles approaching from the right, subject to stated exceptions.
A French zone de rencontre has a 20 km/h limit and pedestrians may use the carriageway with priority over vehicles; cycle directions follow the statutory default subject to local decisions.
Ukraine identifies a residential zone with sign 5.34 and section 26 governs the zone.
